title: Sploitkit Consumables
doc: Slice toggle. Off: Slices.VerdictForOverlay skips every file below before
it is opened, so none of its rows reach RulePlan. These files are loaded
by the row-edit engine, so they also have no effect while [Slices]
ModelRules is off (ModelRules.Init returns before Overlays.Load).
Files this toggle gates:
consumables-sploitkits.csv
ItemClass 6.
ItemModel's consumables are split into six sheets by ItemClass: 1 medical,
2 grenades, 3 devices, 4 chems, 6 sploitkits, 7 matrix. There is no
ItemClass 5.
Lever sheet, not a direct overlay: the first column is ItemName, not a row
id. Consumables.cs owns the whole parse and expands each row at load into
writes on up to three tables: ItemModel keyed on ItemTypeId, TalentModel
keyed on the row's TalentId, and the payload table keyed on the row's
EffectId / MatrixEffectId. Lever cells take blank, =N, +N, -N or xN.
A blank identity cell means the row reaches no row of that table. Unlike
Cyberweapons.cs and Implants.cs, Consumables.cs does not treat that as a
malformed row; a payload cell on such a row is refused and named. A
non-blank, non-integer id refuses the whole row.
The three sploitkits have TalentId 0 and no talent row, so this sheet
carries ItemModel columns only; talent levers here would do nothing.
uiDoc: Turn this off and the mod skips this page's files, so nothing on this page is applied.

fields.label: Enable Sploitkit Consumables
fields.doc: On applies this slice's files; off skips them before they are opened. Default true. Lever sheet, not a direct overlay: the first column is ItemName, and there is no game table called "consumables-sploitkits".
fields.uiDoc: Turn this off and the mod skips this page's files, so nothing on this page is applied.
